items.title: Inventory active Lattice identities, freeze historical evidence, and adopt the superseding clean-break policy
items.context: Before any production edit, inventory each active identity class (root/lab/utils package names, npm bins and wrappers, command text, role IDs, environment keys, state/config/adapter paths, runtime identifiers, hooks, prompts, and docs) and write a superseding decision with per-class canonical-write, compatibility-read, historical-verification, and residue-allowlist rules. Historical stories, legacy migration inputs, compatibility fixtures, changelog records, schemas, signature salts, and provenance/hash-bound bytes remain frozen only where byte stability is required.
items.userSees: The verifier prints `PASS identity-cutover policy: every active legacy identity is classified; frozen evidence allowlist is exact and current` before production migration begins.
excludes: Changing signature salts or provenance-bound schemas

happy.desc: Before the first production migration commit, the superseding cutover decision enumerates root/Lab/Utils package names, bins and wrappers, command text, role IDs, environment keys, state/config/adapter paths, runtime identifiers, hooks, prompts, and current docs, and assigns each occurrence an explicit canonical-only write, remove, or exact frozen-evidence disposition with rationale; the committed verifier reports no unclassified active residue. WHY: proves the clean-break policy precedes implementation and is exhaustive.

edge.desc: Run the residue classifier over all tracked paths and compare every Lattice token to the decision inventory -> active occurrences are classified as migrate/remove, frozen historical or signature-bound occurrences match exact path+token+reason entries, and no directory wildcard or broad substring exemption is accepted. WHY: distinguishes exact active residue from protected history without rewriting either class.

adversarial.desc: On a temporary copy, delete one identity class from the decision, broaden one frozen-evidence entry, or place the decision after a production migration commit -> the cutover verifier fails with the missing class, overbroad exemption, or ordering violation and cannot claim policy completion. WHY: prevents a retrospective or vacuous superseding decision.

items.title: Commit RED regression tests for every active legacy identity class and frozen-history boundary
items.context: Before production edits, commit failing tests that cover @lattice/lab, @lattice/utils, root package identity, npm bin maps and removed wrappers, active command guidance, role/env/path/config canonical-only new writes, and active-file residue. The same RED suite must capture pre-migration historical byte/digest baselines and successful signature verification, then GREEN must prove those bytes/digests and verification results remain unchanged. The residue allowlist must be narrow, reasoned, fail closed when stale, and have mutation proof.
items.userSees: At RED it prints `FAIL identity-cutover: active legacy identities remain` with class diagnostics; at descendant GREEN the same command prints `PASS identity-cutover` while named historical digest/signature checks print `PASS unchanged`.
excludes: Uncommitted ad-hoc grep as the sole RED evidence

happy.desc: At the pre-migration commit, run the committed identity-cutover verifier and bind its non-zero result through red_evidence_create to the exact acceptance target later used for GREEN -> the receipt names each failing active identity class while the explicitly named historical artifacts already pass byte, digest, and signature-verification baselines. WHY: establishes non-fixture RED before production edits without treating protected history as failure.

At a descendant GREEN commit, evaluate the same RED receipt acceptance target -> it passes without changing the receipt target, and its recorded RED commit is an ancestor of GREEN. WHY: proves true RED-to-GREEN lineage rather than replacing the test after implementation.

edge.desc: Before and after changing the self-hosted canonical storyDir/config identity, invoke story_get and checklist_get for B-022e through the canonical proof-or-stop entrypoint -> both phases discover the same story and CHK-001..CHK-008 metadata, and the descendant GREEN run uses the same acceptance target. WHY: makes the self-host transition non-vacuous.

The baseline manifest names each frozen artifact by exact repository-relative path plus byte digest algorithm/value and signature verification command/result -> GREEN reproduces byte-for-byte equality, identical digests, and the same successful verification result. WHY: prevents an anonymous or prose-only history claim.

adversarial.desc: In temporary copies, inject one new active lattice identity, mutate one frozen byte or signature salt, make an allowlist entry stale, or widen it to a directory/glob -> the same verifier fails with a class-specific diagnostic; removing or renaming the RED test also invalidates the receipt. WHY: supplies fail-closed allowlist and mutation proof.

items.title: Migrate Lab, Utils, and root package identities to Proof-or-Stop
items.context: Synchronize manifests, every tracked lockfile, dependency resolution, the global Lab verifier, and packed tarballs. Do not leak unpublished file: dependencies into distributable manifests.
items.userSees: Packed-manifest inspection prints `PASS packages: proof-or-stop, @proof-or-stop/core, @proof-or-stop/lab, @proof-or-stop/utils; no @lattice or file: dependencies`.
excludes: Publishing packages to a remote registry

happy.desc: Build and npm pack the root, main/core, Lab, and Utils workspaces, then inspect every packed package.json and tracked lockfile -> public names/dependencies are proof-or-stop, @proof-or-stop/core, @proof-or-stop/lab, and @proof-or-stop/utils only, versions/resolutions agree, and no distributable manifest contains an unpublished file: dependency. WHY: verifies registry-facing package identity, not only source manifests.

edge.desc: Install only the produced tarballs into a newly created empty temporary project with registry/network fallback disabled -> require/import resolution for each @proof-or-stop package succeeds from packed contents and the global Lab verifier targets the canonical package. WHY: catches workspace-link leakage hidden by the monorepo.

adversarial.desc: From that clean tarball install, resolve @lattice/core, @lattice/lab, and @lattice/utils and inspect dependency trees for @lattice or file: edges -> every legacy resolution fails and no alias/transitive/file dependency reintroduces it; mutating one packed manifest back to @lattice makes the verifier fail. WHY: proves a clean break at the consumer boundary.

items.title: Remove every active lattice command entrypoint and standardize proof-or-stop CLI invocation
items.context: Bins, spawned commands, help, hints, errors, hooks, scripts, agent prompts, and examples must invoke proof-or-stop only. Keep no lattice alias or deprecated command fallback.
items.userSees: The isolated install prints `Proof-or-Stop 0.3.268` for `proof-or-stop --version`; `proof-or-stop help` and `proof-or-stop lab help` succeed; invoking `lattice` prints command-not-found or equivalent non-zero resolution failure.

happy.desc: Install the packed CLI globally into an isolated prefix and enumerate executable bins -> proof-or-stop is the sole product bin; proof-or-stop --version, help, lab help, and representative help/error/hint paths succeed and begin with or teach proof-or-stop only. WHY: verifies the user-visible command surface end to end.

edge.desc: Exercise child-process spawn sites, hooks, package scripts, generated agent instructions, CI examples, and repair hints -> each invokes the canonical proof-or-stop command and none depends on a repository-local deprecated wrapper. WHY: covers indirect entrypoints that a bin-map-only assertion misses.

adversarial.desc: In the isolated install, invoke lattice, search installed bins for a lattice alias, and attempt any deprecated wrapper/fallback path -> command resolution fails, no wrapper file or bin map exists, and adding one alias causes entrypoint/cutover verifiers to fail. WHY: proves removal rather than documentation-only renaming.

items.title: Migrate active runtime identities while preserving historical signatures and evidence
items.context: Move active constants, env/path/role/config identifiers to Proof-or-Stop. Signature salts, schemas, historical stories, and provenance/hash-bound content remain byte-stable; any necessary residue requires a bounded allowlist entry.
items.userSees: Fresh-runtime checks print `PASS canonical identities` and `PASS roles: proof-or-stop-review-story-init and complete proof-or-stop-* registry`; every legacy lattice-* role lookup prints unknown-role and exits non-zero.
excludes: Maintaining read-both compatibility for active runtime identities

happy.desc: Create a fresh isolated project/runtime and invoke canonical init/generation/state/config/adapter paths -> every newly written directory, config key, environment key, runtime identifier, agent role ID, and generated asset uses Proof-or-Stop only; the canonical role registry resolves proof-or-stop-review-story-init and the complete expected proof-or-stop-* role set. WHY: verifies canonical-only fresh writes across runtime surfaces.

Load the canonical package role registry and render each active role -> every registry key, template filename, frontmatter name, config route, and generated role identifier is the expected Proof-or-Stop identity with no omitted active role. WHY: treats Agent identity as runtime identity, not prose.

edge.desc: For every exact historical artifact named in the RED baseline, compare pre-cutover and GREEN bytes/digests and rerun its signature verifier -> byte content and digest are identical and verification still succeeds, while fresh artifacts use only canonical identities. WHY: proves migration did not purchase zero residue by corrupting evidence.

Exercise the self-hosted proof-or-stop.config.json/storyDir transition while querying B-022e and writing fresh nonhistorical metadata -> the active story remains discoverable and new writes land only under the canonical path without a read-both legacy runtime dependency. WHY: proves the running tool survives its own identity migration.

adversarial.desc: Attempt to resolve or generate lattice-review-story-init or any other active lattice-* role ID, legacy env key, state/config path, adapter ID, or runtime identifier -> resolution/generation fails rather than aliasing; injecting one legacy registry key/template/frontmatter/config route makes the verifier fail. WHY: proves old runtime and Agent identities are retired.

On a temporary copy, mutate a frozen provenance byte or signature salt while keeping active residue zero -> history verification fails and blocks GREEN. WHY: prevents the residue objective from overriding evidence integrity.

items.title: Update current source prose, verifiers, adapters, and product documentation
items.context: Update README, CLI docs, templates, adapters, and verification scripts. Preserve original historical decision statements and add a superseding decision instead of rewriting the past.
items.userSees: The residue verifier prints `PASS active prose/assets: Proof-or-Stop only` and `PASS frozen history: unchanged`; regenerated prompts contain no lattice-named active Agent.
excludes: Rewriting prior decision claims in place

happy.desc: Render current README/CLI guidance, templates, adapters, hooks, verifier output, and generated prompts -> all current product prose and examples say Proof-or-Stop/proof-or-stop, and generated active roles expose the exact canonical proof-or-stop-* set including proof-or-stop-review-story-init. WHY: verifies source and generated user surfaces together.

edge.desc: Compare current-source residue findings with the exact frozen-history allowlist -> prior decision/changelog statements remain byte-identical and truthfully superseded, while no current template, registry key, filename, frontmatter name, config route, or generated asset is exempted as history. WHY: preserves honest records without sheltering live assets.

adversarial.desc: Ask agent_prompt/config routing for lattice-review-story-init and every other legacy lattice-* role, and regenerate assets from templates -> old IDs cannot resolve and no legacy filename/frontmatter/registry key is emitted; reintroducing any one of them or rewriting a historical statement makes the prompt-baseline/cutover verifier fail. WHY: proves both negative role resolution and frozen-history boundaries.

items.title: Reach GREEN with builds, package tarballs, clean installs, CLI smoke tests, and residue checks
items.context: Verify main/lab/utils builds; npm pack and clean tarball installs; proof-or-stop --version/help/lab help/lab run; doctor; entrypoint and contract verifiers. Active residue is zero and allowlisted residue is frozen evidence only.
items.userSees: The GREEN transcript ends with `PASS identity-cutover`, successful build/pack/clean-install/CLI/Lab/doctor/contract checks, and legacy command/package/role negative checks all reporting expected non-zero resolution.
excludes: Treating allowlisted historical evidence as active residue

happy.desc: Run main/Lab/Utils builds, identity-cutover, entrypoint, global-Lab, process-fact, runtime-fact, prompt-baseline, and Codex adapter verifiers, then pack and clean-install all artifacts -> proof-or-stop --version/help/lab help/lab run and doctor succeed and the active-residue report is zero. WHY: establishes the complete GREEN product boundary.

edge.desc: With only clean tarball contents available, resolve proof-or-stop and @proof-or-stop/core/lab/utils and execute representative CLI/Lab behavior -> all canonical positives succeed; lattice and @lattice/core/lab/utils fail to resolve, with no workspace source or unpublished file: fallback. WHY: proves installed behavior rather than monorepo behavior.

adversarial.desc: Mutation-test the residue gate by injecting a legacy token into an active file, deleting an exact frozen occurrence, changing an allowlisted token/path, adding a stale allowlist row, and broadening an entry to a glob/directory -> each mutation fails closed with a precise diagnostic while the unmodified tree passes. WHY: demonstrates the zero-residue/allowlist claim is sensitive and non-vacuous.

items.title: Synchronize the patch version and complete REVIEW, TEST, and DONE convergence
items.context: This changes runtime behavior and requires a patch bump. Commit code and evidence, complete review lanes, routine validation, any DONE-required policy, done_prepare, and the local merge to main.
items.userSees: `proof-or-stop --version` reports 0.3.268 and B-022e completes REVIEW, routine validation, required DONE proof, done_prepare, and local merge to main.
excludes: Pushing a task branch or remote main
Declaring completion without product-level clean-install evidence

happy.desc: After all implementation/evidence commits, package.json, package-lock.json, main/Lab/Utils manifests, the canonical brand/version constant, built output, packed --version output, and proof-or-stop --version all agree on 0.3.268; required REVIEW lanes record fresh signed pass evidence, routine proof-or-stop validate passes, configured DONE-required validation passes, done_prepare --mergeMain --refreshStale --validate reports PASS, and story_advance DONE merges locally to main. WHY: proves version and lifecycle convergence at the shipped boundary.

edge.desc: Recompute review, verificationEvidence, validation, DONE-required, delivery, and adapter freshness against the final story-owned files/HEAD after the last generated metadata or main merge -> only admissible current evidence is consumed, head-only unrelated drift follows the CLI freshness classification, and no remote task branch/main push occurs. WHY: prevents a superficially green but stale closeout.

adversarial.desc: From temporary closeout states with one manifest/version constant at 0.3.267, dirty product files, stale validation or DONE-required evidence, missing review lane/pass, open blocking finding, failing clean-install negative, or changed storyFilesHash after review -> build/version verifier or lifecycle gate refuses DONE and names the blocker. WHY: proves REVIEW/TEST/DONE cannot be bypassed by partial version or stale proof.
